people.name: Richard McKay Rorty
people.field: philosopher, historian of ideas, and public intellectual

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: Rorty enrolled at the University of Chicago, where he received a bachelor's and a master's degree in philosophy

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: continuing at Yale University for a PhD in philosophy (1952–1956).

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: Rorty's doctoral dissertation, The Concept of Potentiality, was a historical study of the concept, completed under the supervision of Paul Weiss

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: He married another academic, Amélie Oksenberg (Harvard University professor), with whom he had a son, Jay Rorty, in 1954.

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: he taught at Wellesley College for three years until 1961.

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: Rorty divorced his wife and then married Stanford University bioethicist Mary Varney in 1972.

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: Rorty's academic career included appointments as the Stuart Professor of Philosophy at Princeton University

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: in 1982 he became Kenan Professor of the Humanities at the University of Virginia

relations.subject: Richard McKay Rorty
relations.evidence: In 1998 Rorty became professor of comparative literature (and philosophy, by courtesy), at Stanford University, where he spent the remainder of his academic career.
